preservation.policy: All supplied data is preserved below. Supported normalizations are separate sidecar values; no missing fields are invented.

findings.disposition: Retained R4 as supplied; no replacement source was inferred.

findings.description: R3 is not referenced by either supplied citations or supplied figure credits and is not marked as further reading.
findings.disposition: Retained the record; R1 being cited does not make the separate R3 identifier cited.

findings.description: Two records share R2. Their titles and URLs differ; the latter explicitly identifies a revised edition and supplies year 2026.
findings.disposition: Did not merge records or assign a new identifier. Distinct editions must remain distinguishable.

findings.description: R1 and R3 have identical author, year, title, and DOI. R1 additionally supplies a URL. This is a duplicate-source candidate on supplied metadata, not external proof of source identity.
findings.disposition: Retained both stable IDs and all fields; did not consolidate or copy R1's URL to R3.

findings.description: The R2 citation matches both bibliography records. The supplied material does not establish which edition was intended.
findings.disposition: Left unresolved; did not prefer the record with more complete metadata.

findings.description: The value does not match DOI syntax 10.<4-9 digits>/<non-whitespace suffix>.
findings.disposition: Preserved the value and supplied no canonical DOI or replacement.

findings.description: The original Follow-up Survey record has no year. The year from the revised-edition record cannot safely be transferred.
findings.disposition: No date was invented. Citation-style completeness cannot be certified without an approved style.

findings.description: Background Reading has only an ID, title, and furtherReading flag. No author, year, or source locator is supplied, so the source cannot be identified reliably from this file.
findings.disposition: Kept as intentional further reading, not as an uncited-entry error; no missing metadata was invented.

snapshotValidator.interpretation: Expected issue-detection exit; the audit did not pass cleanly.
snapshotValidator.limits: Checks citation IDs against bibliography, duplicate IDs, and raw DOI syntax only. It does not check figure credits, duplicate-source metadata, citation ambiguity, URLs, missing fields, rights, or rendered placement.

supplementaryValidation.interpretation: Audit consistency and offline metadata checks passed; the underlying bibliography still has the reported errors.

limitations: No network requests were made. HTTP availability, redirects, access restrictions, link content, DOI registration and resolution, and bibliographic accuracy were not verified.
Identifier syntax is not proof that a DOI or source exists, and citation presence is not proof that a claim is true.
Only the JSON citation and credit lists were supplied. Full manuscript citation coverage, note order, citation link text, page references, and all figure/table/image coverage cannot be audited.
No figure assets, rights records, table inventory, or original-analysis statements were supplied. Figure 2's ID resolves, but attribution sufficiency, ownership and reuse rights remain unverified.
No rendered publication was supplied; source-line legibility, placement and attachment to the correct visual object were not inspected.
No approved citation style was supplied. Existing ID-based references were preserved; ID gaps were not treated as broken sequential reference numbering.
Author names, titles, years, publishers and access dates were not expanded, reformatted speculatively, or invented.
